description: Writes the terminal status for one stage. Per ADR-016's write-ordering invariant, the caller must have already committed that stage's own data (e.g. write_enriched for the enrichment stage) before calling this, since a reader polling run_stages must never observe a 'succeeded' stage whose data isn't there yet.
signature: def finish_run_stage(conn: sqlite3.Connection, run_id: str, stage: str, status: str, *, error_message: str | None = None) -> None
docstring:
Transition a running stage to a terminal status.

Args:
    conn: An open connection.
    run_id: The run this stage belongs to.
    stage: One of 'acquisition', 'enrichment', 'analysis'.
    status: One of 'succeeded', 'failed', 'cancelled'. Not 'pending' or 'running' -- those are begin_run_stage's job.
    error_message: Populated when status is 'failed' or 'cancelled' with a cause; ignored (but not rejected) for 'succeeded'.

Returns:
    None.

Raises:
    StorageError: If run_id/stage has no row at all (finish before begin), or status is not one of the three terminal values.
preconditions: A run_stages row for (run_id, stage) already exists (created by a prior begin_run_stage call)
The stage's own data writes (write_enriched / write_analysis_result / acquisition's raw_games writes) are already committed
postconditions: read_run_stages(conn, run_id) shows the row with the given status and finished_at set
error_message is stored verbatim when provided
The write is committed before finish_run_stage returns

edge_cases.input: stage was never begun (no row exists)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: StorageError -- recording a terminal status with no start time would be a caller bug, not a valid state; this differs from delete_run's no-op-on-unknown-id contract because a mismatched begin/finish call pair signals an orchestration bug worth surfacing loudly
accepted and stored; storage does not enforce that error_message is only set for failure states, since a caller might attach a non-fatal warning summary even on success
StorageError -- finish_run_stage only accepts the three terminal values, use begin_run_stage to (re)enter 'running'

edge_cases.input: finish_run_stage called twice for the same (run_id, stage) without an intervening begin_run_stage
edge_cases.expected_behavior: the second call succeeds and overwrites the terminal status and finished_at -- storage enforces no state-machine transition rules, matching update_run_status's own documented latitude

unit_tests.name: test_finish_succeeded_sets_terminal_state
unit_tests.description: A begun stage finished with 'succeeded' shows finished_at set and error_message None.
unit_tests.expected: read_run_stages shows status='succeeded', finished_at not None

unit_tests.name: test_finish_failed_stores_error_message
unit_tests.description: status='failed' with an error_message stores it verbatim.
unit_tests.expected: read_run_stages shows status='failed' with that exact error_message

unit_tests.name: test_finish_never_begun_raises
unit_tests.description: Calling finish_run_stage for a (run_id, stage) with no existing row raises StorageError.

unit_tests.name: test_invalid_status_raises
unit_tests.description: status='running' is rejected as not a terminal value.
